title: Sections on a finite open-and-closed coproduct in a small etale site
statement: Let S be a scheme and let F be a sheaf of sets on the small etale site of S [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. Let X be an object of that site, and suppose given finitely many objects X_i and open-and-closed coprojections j_i : X_i \to X such that X is their coproduct [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], X_i \times_X X_k is empty for i != k, and F(empty) is a singleton. Then {j_i} is a covering and restriction induces a bijection F(X) \to product_i F(X_i), with inverse given by the unique gluing of a compatible family; under this bijection, restriction along j_i is the i-th projection.

source.place: Tag 03SF, finite Galois descent calculation (sections on the finite disjoint union)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], each coprojection $j_i$ is an open immersion with pairwise disjoint images whose union is $X$. Open immersions are etale (Stacks Tag 02GP), so the finite family $\{j_i\}$ is a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms, hence a covering in the small etale site described by [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. Its fibre products $X_i\times_X X_k$ for $i\ne k$ are empty because the images are disjoint; since an open immersion is a monomorphism, the two projections $X_i\times_X X_i\to X_i$ coincide (both are the inverse of the diagonal isomorphism).

source.place: Tag 03SF, finite Galois descent calculation (the finite disjoint-union covering by the coproduct components)

proof.text: Apply the equalizer condition in [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] to the covering in Step 1. For $i\ne k$ the overlap $X_i\times_X X_k$ is empty and $\mathcal F(\emptyset)$ is a singleton (the sheaf condition for the empty covering of the empty object), so the two restrictions to it agree for every family; for $i=k$ the two projections $X_i\times_X X_i\to X_i$ coincide by Step 1, so the two restrictions agree as well. Hence compatibility imposes no condition on a family $(s_i)_i$. Thus restriction $\mathcal F(X)\to\prod_i\mathcal F(X_i)$ is bijective, with inverse the unique glued section; by construction its composite with the $i$-th restriction is the $i$-th projection. The same argument covers the empty finite family, where both sides are singleton sets.
